gaps.sentence: He passed all his exams first time, ___ surprised everyone.
gaps.hint: refers to the whole previous clause
gaps.explanation: 'Which' can refer to a whole idea ('he passed first time'); this non-defining use never takes 'that'.

gaps.sentence: That's exactly ___ I needed — thank you!
gaps.explanation: 'What I needed' means 'the thing that I needed'; 'that' cannot be used in this free relative position.

gaps.sentence: All ___ I want is a quiet weekend at home.
gaps.explanation: After 'all' the relative pronoun is 'that' (often omitted); 'all what' is always wrong.

gaps.sentence: The author, about ___ there has been much debate, will speak at the festival.
gaps.hint: debate about the author — person after preposition
gaps.explanation: 'About whom' is required after the preposition 'about' when referring to a person.

gaps.sentence: The house ___ stands on the corner dates from 1870.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' is needed because a house is a thing; 'where' would introduce information about location, not a subject.

gaps.sentence: Nobody explained the reason ___ the flight was cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'Why' introduces the cause after 'the reason'; it means 'for which'.

gaps.sentence: The man ___ lives next door is a doctor.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to people as the subject of the clause; 'which' is for things and 'whose' shows possession.

gaps.sentence: The programme ___ I watched last night was about volcanoes.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to things, even when it is the object of the clause.
